title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT with a cyclotomic-squaring branch, success target 0.39

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with M=2^20 walks, R=1024 partitions and theta=2^-60) succeeds with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.585 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000). The walk mixes two step types on the class space: with probability s=35/64 (a fixed 6-bit field of the free class invariant T0=Re(c_0), the Fp part of the w^0 coefficient, which is equal on all 12 Frobenius conjugates and costs no multiplication) the step is y<-y^2 by cyclotomic squaring, valid on GT and commuting with Frobenius, with exponents (alpha,beta)<-(2alpha,2beta) mod r; otherwise it is one twisted-table multiplication y<-y*T[h][t] with the twelve conjugate keys computed from four Fp multiplications, the partition h taken from ten bits of T0 and the twist t from kappa, as in the published Frobenius-class rho design. The three per-step decision fields (partition bits 0..9, branch bits 10..15, distinguished bits 16..75 of T0) are disjoint bit ranges of one class invariant, so outside cycle handling every per-step decision is a function of the current class and two walks at one class take the same step, while the two cycle escapes are functions of the cycle reached rather than of the walker (the 2-cycle escape squares the smaller-T0 class, the checkpoint escape walks the cycle to its smallest-T0 class and squares it), so two walks that reach one cycle compute the same escape class and action and their class sequences coincide from their first common class onward, coalescing within one cycle length; a squaring step computes no class key, and the 128-bit report key is derived from the class key K, computed at a report and charged there. The 2-cycle and checkpoint comparisons run on every step and compare T0 (381 bits; a false match has probability about 2^-380.70 per comparison, total below 2^-253, and can only cause a spurious escape, never a false logarithm, because the report key comes from K). The squaring step is measured, not modelled, and the measurement ships in the package's measure/ directory (harness, raw Callgrind records, exact totals, disassembly audit; experiment.py re-derives them): blst's blst_fp12_cyclotomic_sqr at revision f7a88067 costs 9,803.0 executed instructions per call ((I65-I1)/64) on the track's own COST_MODEL toolchain, identical at five slice offsets over five different GT elements and input-independent because the routine is straight-line (18 functions, 1,017 static instructions, zero conditional, backward or indirect branches); the ledger charges the body 9,803-5=9,798, the 5 being loop control the common rows already charge. The same harness reproduces blst_fp_mul=383.0 and blst_fp12_mul=22,996.0 exactly, and on GT elements the routine equals blst_fp12_sqr. The charge is 10,098 instructions = 0.50490 units (9,798 plus 300 for the alpha/beta doubling, the shared rows and slack); with that price the W-minimising branch fraction is s=35/64, the best 2^-k bit field near the optimum 0.5461. Collision law: squaring is injective on classes (|GT| is odd) so squaring-squaring pairs never merge, squaring-multiply pairs merge at about 1/N, and multiply-multiply pairs at about (1-1/(12R))/N, giving N'=N/(1-s^2-(1-s)^2/R)=2^251.785202, charged with 1/R instead of 1/(12R) in the third term (which makes N' larger by 3.78 x 10^-4 in log2), S0'=sqrt(2N'ln(1/0.61))=2^125.884326 and S=1.03 S0'=2^125.926969 steps. Fruitless cycles are all-multiply only: a cycle with t>=1 squaring steps multiplies the exponent pair by 2^t p^m, which is 1 mod r only when ord_r(2)=(r-1)/16=2^250.857 divides 12t, i.e. t>=2^247.27 (both computed in experiment.py part A), so the fruitless-cycle rates carry their (1-s)^L factors (0.0101 R^-2 for L=3..64 against 0.1391 R^-2 without the branch) and the ledger nonetheless charges the unbranched R^-2 with 200 steps per event. Within-walk returns are handled events, not a failure: algebraic fruitless 2-cycles occur at rate (1-s)^2/(12R)=1.67 x 10^-5 per step (of order 2^110.1 over the run), and each is detected by the T0 comparison two steps back and escaped by squaring the smaller-T0 class; checkpoint cycles of length 3..64 are detected by the 64-step ring and escaped the same way; both are charged inside the overhead factor, and the escape is a function of the cycle reached, not of the walker. Every other revisit is a tail collision: with different exponent pairs it is the useful collision, and with equal pairs it is a class cycle longer than the checkpoint window, which needs all-multiply steps and has probability below 2^-100. The failure list therefore carries no birthday term for within-walk returns, and the report log's capacity rests on the deterministic per-slot cap R_w=2^47, C_rep=M R_w=2^67, not on any assumption about returns. Because the branch bit is a function of the class, revisits repeat an earlier decision and step costs are not i.i.d. across time, so the slot's work is accounted by type: productive steps on newly exposed classes take i.i.d. costs in [0.50490, 1.1125] with mean 0.78021875 (H1 supplies a fresh draw there), tail revisits are O(1) (S^2/(2N')=0.524) and get a deterministic 2^80-step per-slot allowance, and cycle handling is charged at 8.35 times its measured mixed rate. The meter is a private 128-bit instruction counter with hard cap W_cap=2^119.871882, so all walk work is at most M x (W_cap-1+20,000+2,250)=2^125.584170 units as a deterministic bound; Hoeffding bounds a slot's productive work above 1.01 of nominal by 2^(-2^94.89) (2^(-2^114.89) over the run - 94.89 is the exponent of the exponent, not a probability) and the cycle charge is beaten only with probability 2^(-2^94.76), so all S productive steps survive except with probability below 2^-100, and the separate 0.01 success allowance is slack for the heuristic parts of the model. The report machinery is direct-addressed: a log of exactly M R_w = 2^20 x 2^47 = 2^67 records of 80 bytes, an append rule that stores no repeat of the walk's last record and runs both cycle checks first, a per-slot cumulative report counter carried across restarts and stopping the slot at R_w, matched offline by an in-place heapsort of the whole 80-byte record (at most 67 levels at 130 instructions per record, budgeted 10,000) with one adjacent 80-byte comparison per record for duplicate removal (so byte-identical records from two walkers are collapsed before pairing and a coincident pair is never divided on) and at most one 200-instruction charge per pair of the remaining distinct records of an equal-key run, against a hard pair budget P=2^41 whose abort probability is at most 2^-36 by Markov over the about 2^5 expected false-key pairs; the first pair of equal canonical elements with different exponent pairs gives x=(A1-A2)/(B2-B1) mod r and the output is verified by e(P,Q)=z. Peak memory is below 2^73.4 bytes (a hard bound: 2^67 records of 80 bytes plus the multiplier table and the walk states, with no hash table, no chaining and no eviction); preprocessing and table construction are at most 2^57 group-operation equivalents, including the 2^56.30-unit initialization of all 2^67 log records, all included in W; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound is 0.40808 (model at 1.03 S0', rounded down) minus the 0.01 allowance minus 2^-18 of loss terms >= 0.3980 >= 0.39, and rests on the standard random-mapping heuristic for the mixed walk (branch-adjusted Brent-Pollard correction, 3% step slack), the same heuristic behind the section-3.2 cycle rates and the report-cap margin (mean 2^45.927 reports per slot against the cap 2^47, a ratio of 2.1038); it is supported by toy-field experiments that run the production fields from T0, squaring, step order, append rule, work meter and matcher, plus a direct measurement of the branch-adjusted collision law; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements, check GT membership, the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula and its distinctness, that the two-subtraction sign-set minimum equals the twelve-way argmin and class key, that kappa selects the same canonical representative from all 12 conjugates, p^6 = inversion, ord_r(p) = 12, the factorisation of r-1 and ord_r(2) = (r-1)/16 with the smallest t that a fruitless cycle could contain, that T0 = Re(c_0) is equal on all 12 conjugates, and that Granger-Scott cyclotomic squaring equals y*y with its Fp multiplication/addition/subtraction counts measured by running it. Part A2: frequencies of the 76 used bits of T0 (partition, branch and distinguished fields) and of the 128 record-key bits of the class key K on real GT elements, plus the measured branch-field and distinguished-field fractions. Part P: the production step rule on real GT elements with a 16-entry table, two walkers started at two different conjugates of one element, which must produce the same T0 sequence, with the exponent invariant y = g^alpha z^beta checked for both and the squaring fraction, multiply steps, reports and key computations counted. Part E: the branch-adjusted collision law measured directly in the toy field q = 67 by sampling distinct classes, applying one step to each and counting image coincidences by pair type, compared with 1 - s^2 - (1-s)^2/(12R) and with the charged 1 - s^2 - (1-s)^2/R, with squaring-squaring coincidences required to be exactly zero. Part B: the complete mixed walk (T0 bit fields, Granger-Scott squaring, four-multiplication keys only on multiply steps, 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes on T0, stuck-walk rule, append rule, per-slot report cap, per-slot work meter) in three toy fields near 2^20 with the production step order, every trial run to the fixed step budget 1.03 S0', then the production offline matcher (full 80-byte-record sort, adjacent dedup, charged equal-key pairs against a hard pair budget, element recomputation, exponentiation check), with stress passes for the report cap, the stuck-walk restart with the carried slot counter, the work meter and the pair budget. Part C: the bound arithmetic of proof.md, including the zero-sum probabilities, the fruitless-cycle rates with and without the branch, the measured cyclotomic-squaring price against the counted rows, the branch fraction, N', S0', the deterministic report-log capacity, the KL report-cap margin, the memory bound, the per-record report charge, the hard pair budget, the work-meter cap as an exact integer, its Hoeffding concentration exponent, the counter-width table, and an exact integer check that the claim is log2 W rounded up at three decimals. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs or production key statistics.
